samples.summary: stampSource ignores `ambiguous` from findJsxRoots, so a duplicated root name both loses one function's stamps and emits ids resolveNode can never resolve
samples.evidence: `findJsxRoots` deliberately reports duplicate names in `ambiguous` (jsx-nodes.mjs:451) and `resolveNode` refuses them outright (jsx-nodes.mjs:655-660), but `addRoot` still does `roots[name] = root`, keeping only the LAST function under that name. `stampSource` at stamp.mjs:85 iterates `Object.entries(roots)` with no reference to `ambiguous`. Two consequences on the exact shape the module's own test fixture uses (`function One(){ const Row = () => <li/>; …} function Two(){ const Row = () => <td/>; …}`, jsx-nodes.test.mjs:~470): (1) every JSX element of the FIRST `Row` is never stamped at all, so a click on one of its rendered DOM nodes finds no `data-wb-node` on itself and falls back to the nearest stamped ancestor — i.e. selects a different source node, silently, which is the precise failure the module header says it exists to prevent; (2) every id that IS stamped is prefixed `Row:`, and any anchor built from it is unconditionally rejected by `resolveNode` with "more than one JSX-returning function is named Row", so those elements look selectable but can never be written. Ambiguity is treated as absence in the resolver and as ordinary success in the stamper.

samples.summary: requireStatic permits a structural edit on a top-level returned element, where a sibling splice produces invalid JSX
samples.evidence: For a child of the synthetic returns root, `childrenOf` calls `pushExpr(j, parentScope, out, j)` (line 261), so `owner === node`, and the scope is `static`. Both `requireStatic` guards (lines 699 and 712) therefore pass for path `[0]`. But a returns-root child is the whole return expression: splicing a sibling next to it yields `return <div/><span/>`, which is not valid JSX, and deleting it turns the function into a component that returns nothing. The guard blocks the `{cond && <x/>}` case and the iteration case but has no case for "this node is a return value, not a member of a parent element's child list". Any `layout-insert`/`layout-remove` targeting path `[0]` is accepted and will corrupt the file. (`inject.mjs` is not in the tree yet, hence medium confidence about the consuming call site, but the guard as written does not refuse it.)

samples.summary: resolveNode dereferences client-supplied `anchor.path` with no validation — a missing or non-array path throws TypeError instead of returning `located: false`
samples.evidence: `resolveNode` is documented as the server-side guard for client-supplied anchors ('the client's SceneMeta can be stale', line 640-642). It immediately does `entries.find((e) => samePath(e.path, anchor.path))` where `samePath` reads `b.length` and `a.every(...)` (line 624); if `anchor.path` is undefined/null/not an array this throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')`. The same value is dereferenced again in the failure message at lines 685 and in the requireStatic messages. samples.summary: classLiteralOf returns the first string literal ANYWHERE in the className expression, which for common cn()/clsx() shapes is an object key or a conditional branch, not the authored class blob
samples.evidence: The visitor at lines 194-202 does a pre-order `forEachChild` walk and stops at the first `StringLiteral`/`NoSubstitutionTemplateLiteral`. The doc claims this is 'the authored class blob in every shadcn/cn() call', which holds only for `cn("base", …)`. For `className={cn({ "is-open": open }, "base")}` the first literal reached is the OBJECT PROPERTY NAME `"is-open"`; for `className={cn(compact ? "p-1" : "p-4", "base")}` it is the ternary branch `"p-1"`. Since this node is what a class edit rewrites in place, an edit would silently overwrite a conditional class key or one branch of a conditional — corrupting behaviour, not just styling. It also feeds `attrsOf().className` and hence `fpx`, so the search key is derived from the wrong token. There is no guard restricting the search to top-level call arguments.

samples.summary: fpOf builds its hash payload from unescaped separators, so identity-attribute values containing `|`, `;`, `,` or `>` can make two different nodes share a fingerprint
samples.evidence: `idStr` joins `name=value` pairs with `;` (line 579) and the payload joins fields with `|` (line 586); `ancestorTags` joins with `>` and `attrNames` with `,`. Identity values come from `init.expression.getText()` or a raw string literal, i.e. arbitrary source text — e.g. `id={a || b}` yields `a || b`, `aria-label="one;two"` yields a literal `;`. Two structurally different nodes can therefore serialise to the identical payload and get the same `fp`. Because `resolveNode`'s relocation step resolves on a UNIQUE `fp` match (line 677), a collision does not surface as ambiguity — it resolves to the wrong node and writes there silently, which the module calls 'the worst failure this tool can have'.

samples.summary: An anonymous or re-exported default export registers no root, making the whole file unaddressable
samples.evidence: Roots are registered only for named `FunctionDeclaration`s (line 457) and for `VariableStatement` initialisers that are arrow/function expressions (line 464-472). `export default () => <div/>`, `export default function () {}` and `export { Page as default }` match none of these: no root is added and `defaultExport` stays null (the `isExportAssignment` branch at 474 only fires for `export default Identifier`). For such a file `findJsxRoots` returns an empty `roots`, so `stampSource` emits nothing and every anchor into it fails with 'no JSX-returning function named …'. No error distinguishes 'unsupported export shape' from 'stale anchor'.

samples.summary: requireStatic's refusal message blames a `{…}` expression for cases where none exists (top-level ternary, double-parenthesised return)
samples.evidence: The `hit.owner !== hit.node` branch (line 712) hardcodes the reason 'sits inside a {…} expression'. But `owner !== node` also arises with no braces at all: `return ok ? <A/> : <B/>` reaches both branches through `pushExpr`'s conditional case (line 329-332) with `owner` = the ternary, and `return ((<div/>))` leaves an extra ParenthesizedExpression as owner because `take` (line 418) unwraps only one level. The refusal itself is right; the diagnostic points the author at syntax that is not in their file.

samples.summary: The singular '1 candidate' branch of the failure message is unreachable
samples.evidence: Control only reaches line 680-688 when `hit` is null, and `hit` is null only when `uniq(entries.filter(e => e.fp === anchor.fp))` returned null, i.e. when the fp match count is 0 or >= 2. `matches.length === 1` can never hold, so `${matches.length === 1 ? '' : 's'}` always renders the plural.

samples.summary: The `seen` offset guard silently drops an id rather than surfacing the overlap it exists to catch
samples.evidence: `if (seen.has(offset)) continue;` (line 100) skips both the edit AND the `stamped.push`, so if two roots ever did reach the same element the returned `stamped` list would quietly omit one id — and the comment says callers use that list to 'assert them against metadata'. Since the comment asserts the overlap cannot happen, a throw (or at least recording the collision) would turn a broken invariant into a visible failure instead of a shorter list.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. jsx-nodes.mjs:450-453 `addRoot` does `roots[name] = root` unconditionally after recording the collision in `ambiguous`, so a duplicated root name keeps only the LAST function. jsx-nodes.mjs:650-660 shows resolveNode destructures `ambiguous` and hard-refuses any anchor whose component is ambiguous. stamp.mjs:74 destructures only `{ roots }` and stamp.mjs:85 iterates `Object.entries(roots)`; the word `ambiguous` appears nowhere in stamp.mjs (whole 121-line file read). Both claimed consequences follow: (1) the first same-named function's JSX is never walked (nested-function JSX is unreachable from the outer root, per stamp.mjs:80-82), so those elements are unstamped and a click falls back to the nearest stamped ancestor — the wrong source node, silently, which is the failure the module header at stamp.mjs:6-9 says it exists to prevent; (2) ids that are emitted carry the ambiguous prefix and any anchor built on that component is rejected at jsx-nodes.mjs:655. No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described; the package contains only jsx-nodes.mjs and stamp.mjs so no intermediate guard filters ambiguous names before the stamping loop; and dropped stamps plus unresolvable ids are a logic/invariant defect in the Correctness lane. stamp.test.mjs has no duplicate-name coverage, and its expectedIds helper (stamp.test.mjs:32) reproduces the same blind spot. The only mitigation found is that no `?wbFrame=` Vite plugin wiring exists in the tree yet, which is a reachability nuance rather than a demonstration that the path is unreachable by design.

verdict.reason: The code the finding describes is real — `samePath` (jsx-nodes.mjs:624) reads `b.length`/`a.every`, and `resolveNode` passes `anchor.path` straight into it (line 666) and `.join('.')`s it at line 685 with no shape check; no `Array.isArray`/typeof guard exists anywhere in packages/design-editor. However, the premise that makes it blocking — a client-supplied anchor crossing a server boundary — does not exist in this repository. `packages/design-editor` contains only three source files (src/server/jsx-nodes.mjs, src/server/stamp.mjs, src/types.ts). A repo-wide grep for `resolveNode` returns only test call sites (test/server/jsx-nodes.test.mjs:56,366,375,382,394,403,410,423,440,453) and docs prose; a repo-wide grep for `jsx-nodes` finds no importer outside the package and none under .trusted/. The `extract.mjs`/`inject.mjs`/plugin route named in the module header do not exist and are listed as pending in docs/tasks/active/20260729-design-editor-layout-sandbox-todo.md. There is no HTTP handler or JSON deserialization feeding this function. Additionally the parameter is contractually typed `path: number[]` (line 645) in a `// @ts-check` file whose typechecking is deliberately enabled per packages/design-editor/tsconfig.json:28-44, so an in-repo checked consumer passing a non-array would fail typecheck rather than reach line 666. Every actual caller today passes well-formed `number[]`. There is therefore no real runtime path on which the TypeError fires; this is defensive hardening for a boundary that has not been built yet (nit/minor), not a crash on a real path, so it does not meet the Correctness lens's blocking bar. I did not find a counterexample guard, so the absence itself stands — the refutation is on blocking-ness, not on the fact.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as the finding describes. `classLiteralOf` (packages/design-editor/src/server/jsx-nodes.mjs:184-206) falls back to an unrestricted pre-order `ts.forEachChild` walk (lines 193-202) that returns the first `StringLiteral`/`NoSubstitutionTemplateLiteral` found anywhere inside the className expression, with no restriction to top-level call arguments. Because TS visits a PropertyAssignment's `name` before its `initializer`, `className={cn({ "is-open": open }, "base")}` yields the object key `"is-open"`; because a ConditionalExpression visits `whenTrue` before `whenFalse`, `cn(compact ? "p-1" : "p-4", "base")` yields `"p-1"`. Both shapes are unguarded and untested (the only cn() test, test/server/jsx-nodes.test.mjs:628-632, covers the benign `cn("a b", other && "c")` shape). The result feeds `attrsOf().className` (lines 164-167) and thence `fpxOf` via `walkNode` (lines 536, 547), so the search key is derived from a token that may be a conditional key rather than the authored class blob, while the documented contract (lines 173-179) declares this node the class-edit target. I found no guard elsewhere that constrains the walk, so `already-guarded` does not apply; the code is present so `not-present` does not apply; and wrong-node selection is squarely in the correctness lane so `out-of-scope` does not apply. The sole mitigator is that no rewriting consumer (inject.mjs) exists in this tree yet, making the corruption impact latent rather than unreal — that is not a named refutation ground.
